target_customer: Enterprise security and vendor risk teams assessing AI vendors, including law firms, healthcare and SaaS companies
problem: Companies adopt AI vendors and agents without visibility into prompt injection, data training and exfiltration risk. PromptArmor assesses and monitors third-party AI risk.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for AI vendor risk intelligence

founders.name: Shankar Krishnan
education: UC Berkeley, Data Science and Economics

founders.name: Vikram Jayanthi
education: UC Berkeley, Computer Science and Public Policy
founders.background_notes: Infrastructure and security roles per the YC page.

competitors.name: Lakera
competitors.what: Protects LLM applications from malicious prompts, launched with Gandalf prompt injection game data

competitors.name: HiddenLayer
competitors.what: Machine learning and generative AI security
competitors.traction_then: Not stated in the source found

technical_complexity.rationale: Assessing AI vendors needs security research and a monitoring pipeline, with an emerging attack class (prompt injection) that few teams understood in 2023.

defensibility.rationale: A research reputation and an accumulating vendor risk database help, but the space drew many funded entrants and acquirers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Per 2026 roundups, Lakera and Prompt Security were acquired (Check Point, SentinelOne) and Protect AI went into Palo Alto, so the category consolidated. PromptArmor itself was not acquired in sources found.

market_need_then: LLM adoption in 2023 raised new security concerns, and press such as Axios in September 2023 described a startup market forming around AI security.

identity.voice_and_tone: Security research voice, publishes named threat research on vendor products

branding.brand_signature: Public threat research on products such as Notion AI and Claude Cowork
branding.community_and_virality: Its Notion AI exfiltration write-up of January 2026 was picked up by Hacker News aggregators and trade write-ups.

brand_strength.rationale: Research disclosures drew third-party coverage, which builds credibility. The name is easily confused with Prompt Security, a different company.

outcome_analysis: PromptArmor is Active and sells to named enterprise and law firm customers, and its public threat research builds credibility. The AI security category is consolidating through acquisitions of rivals, which raises both competitive pressure and exit odds. Funding could not be verified from primary sources.
notes: Funding unverified and conflicting: CB Insights and Extruct list $500K (April 2024, YC); StartupIntros lists a $3M seed in April 2024; VCBacked and Zerogtalent list $3.2M. Aggregators only, so no round recorded. Do not confuse with Prompt Security (acquired by SentinelOne). HiddenLayer entry as a competitor has no traction or funding figure in the cited Axios snippet. Product has pivoted toward AI vendor risk from the earlier LLM security framing, but no dated source, so not recorded as a pivot. Completeness pass: two single-database rounds are recorded as reported: CB Insights 500K seed dated 2024-03-13 and Startupintros 3M seed dated 2024-04-01 (VCBacked shows 3.2M total). They conflict and may describe the same round or the YC deal versus a later close; do not sum them.
